questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to live in a city full of history and atmosphere. I had also heard great things about the University of Edinburgh.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. The study abroad office was very helpful, and they sent detailed emails whenever they needed us to do something.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received information from the study abroad office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used the University of Edinburgh's official site to find student accommodation. It was very easy, and I quickly got an offer. I didn't get into any of my top priorities, but it turned out to be a nice place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any problems with the student housing, and it was very close to the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing with the drop/add-period at the beginning of the semester, but the student office was very helpful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for courses before getting to Edinburgh, but in the first month of the semester, I could still choose to change them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The study abroad office was quick to reply to my questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get into any of my top priorities, so I had to broaden my search a bit.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be flexible regarding courses, because most likely you won't get all your top priorities.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was slightly below what I was used to at my home university. I found the courses and the assignments quite easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At my host institution I only had small seminar classes of about 10-15 people. There was a great emphasis on class discussion. Sometimes I missed the lecture format of my home institution, but the class discussions did help me participate more.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Saints and Sinners - Voicing Belief, Doubt and Dissent in Medieval English Literature
Traditional Song - Gaelic
Edinburgh in Fiction/Fiction in Edinburgh

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend applying for courses that are unique to the host institution. I decided to do some very Scottish-oriented courses since I wouldn't have that opportunity back home. It added to my overall experience that I was learning a lot about the country and city I was living in.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Since I took mainly literature classes, there were quite a lot of books to buy. Also, although it wasn't unexpected, the room I rented was quite expensive considering how relatively small it was.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and public transport was quite cheap. It was really cheap joining student societies as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were all kinds of activities and groups for students, which was a great way of being social and getting to know people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend other exhange students to join one or more student societies since it's a great way of meeting people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel! Scotland is an amazing country for nature lovers. I spent many weekends traveling the Highlands, and it was great.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. I speak English, so there was no real barrier.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The best way of meeting local students would be at your courses, student societies, or at your student housing.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Going to traditional dances, ceilidhs! And exploring the countryside.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do it! It's worth it, you won't regret it. Although you might not get exactly the courses you hoped for, it'll all work out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to the study abroad office, they'll help you navigate the drop/add-period. I visited their office several times and they were always helpful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Several of my courses were excellent. But perhaps the greatest thing was to travel Scotland and meet a lot of new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Perhaps adjusting to the very discussion-based approach to teaching at my courses. And the grading system! I still don't understand it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
